title: A Game at Wrigley Field
fa_title: یک بازی در ورزشگاه ریگلی فیلد

sents.t: On Sunday, Emma took us to see the Chicago Cubs at Wrigley Field.
The stadium opened in 1914, and fans have been cheering there for more than a hundred years.
“I’ve been wanting to come here since I moved,” Emma said.
“My dad has been a Cubs fan all his life.”
The stadium was smaller than I expected, and the outfield walls were covered in green ivy.
Some people were watching the game from the rooftops of buildings across the street.
We bought hot dogs and peanuts, and Lily tried to explain the rules.
“I’ve been watching baseball with Carlos all summer,” she said proudly.
But when a player hit the ball high into the air, she asked, “Is that good?”
During the seventh-inning stretch, the whole stadium stood up and sang “Take Me Out to the Ball Game” together.
In the eighth inning, the Cubs were losing by one run.
Then their best hitter came to bat.
The ball flew over the ivy wall.
Forty thousand people went crazy, and a stranger hugged me.
After the game, we bought Emma a Cubs cap.
“Now you’re a real Chicagoan,” Lily said.

comp.q: How long have fans been cheering at Wrigley Field?
o: for more than a hundred years
comp.fa: هواداران چه مدت است در ریگلی فیلد تشویق می‌کنند؟
چه چیزی دیوارهای زمین بیرونی را پوشانده است؟

comp.q: Where were some people watching the game from?
o: from the rooftops across the street
comp.fa: بعضی‌ها از کجا بازی را تماشا می‌کردند؟

comp.q: Why is Lily’s question “Is that good?” funny?
o: She was talking to a stranger.
She had just said she knew baseball well.
comp.fa: چرا سؤال لیلی «Is that good?» خنده‌دار است؟

comp.q: What does “a close game” mean here?
o: The scores are almost the same.
The game was near their home.

comp.q: What happened in the eighth inning?
o: A Cubs player hit a home run.
comp.fa: در اینینگ هشتم چه اتفاقی افتاد؟
